chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-ala, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Jibraeel (peace be upon him) advised me with the women until I thought that it is not befitting to divorce her except due to manifest immorality'.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for divorcing a wife according to this hadith from al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the Prophetic tradition of prioritizing marital stability, where Jibraeel’s persistent advice led the Prophet to view divorce as a last resort reserved for clear misconduct (fahisha). Shia scholars, such as Al-Majlisi, interpret this as establishing a high evidentiary threshold for divorce, thereby protecting the wife’s rights and discouraging arbitrary separation. This narration underscores the sanctity of the marital bond in Shia jurisprudence, framing divorce not as a casual right but as a necessary measure only when the marriage’s core purpose is compromised.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al A’ala, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> advised me<sup>saww</sup> with the women until I<sup>saww</sup> thought that it is not befitting to divorce her except due to manifest immorality’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from al-‘Ala’ from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Jibril advised me about women (so much) that I began to think of divorce as an improper act unless it is because of openly proven indecency.’”
